reference_sql:
SELECT product_id, week_start, units,
  LAG(units) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY week_start) AS prev_units
FROM weekly_units
WHERE product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 20
  AND week_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-06' AND DATE '2025-06-23'
alternatives:
SELECT w.product_id, w.week_start, w.units, p.units AS prev_units
FROM weekly_units w
LEFT JOIN weekly_units p
  ON p.product_id = w.product_id
 AND p.week_start = w.week_start - INTERVAL 7 DAY
 AND p.week_start >= DATE '2025-01-06'
WHERE w.product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 20
  AND w.week_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-06' AND DATE '2025-06-23'

SELECT product_id, week_start, units,
  LAG(units, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY week_start) AS prev_units
FROM weekly_units
WHERE product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 20
  AND week_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-06' AND DATE '2025-06-23'

other_way.sql:
SELECT w.product_id, w.week_start, w.units, p.units AS prev_units
FROM weekly_units w
LEFT JOIN weekly_units p
  ON p.product_id = w.product_id
 AND p.week_start = w.week_start - INTERVAL 7 DAY
 AND p.week_start >= DATE '2025-01-06'
WHERE w.product_id BETWEEN 1 AND 20
  AND w.week_start BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-06' AND DATE '2025-06-23'
other_way.tradeoff: A self-join on the week 7 days earlier works because every week has a row; with gaps in the weeks, LAG and the join would differ.
